Snowflake - Composio Toolkit | Composio All Toolkits Snowflake SNOWFLAKE Latest version 20261101_00 Snowflake is a cloud-based data warehouse offering elastic scaling, secure data sharing, and SQL analytics across multiple cloud environments Copy page Authentication Details Composio-managed OAuth not available OAuth2 Frequently Asked Questions How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Snowflake? Snowflake has no Composio-managed OAuth app, so you create an OAuth security integration in your own Snowflake account and use its credentials in Composio. Snowflake has no web form for this; you create the integration with SQL. Create the Snowflake OAuth integration You need the ACCOUNTADMIN role, or a role with the privilege to create integrations. Sign in to Snowflake and open a SQL worksheet. Run this command to create a confidential OAuth client that points at Composio: CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION oauth_custom_all_roles
  TYPE = oauth
  ENABLED = true
  OAUTH_CLIENT = custom
  OAUTH_CLIENT_TYPE = 'CONFIDENTIAL'
  OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI = 'https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add'
  OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS = TRUE
  OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY = 7776000; OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI must exactly match the oauth_redirect_uri field in your Composio auth config. Run DESC SECURITY INTEGRATION oauth_custom_all_roles; and copy the OAUTH_CLIENT_ID value. Run the following command and copy the OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET value from the result: SELECT SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS('OAUTH_CUSTOM_ALL_ROLES') AS SECRETS; Create the auth config in Composio In the Composio dashboard, go to Auth Configs , click Create Auth Config , and select Snowflake . Keep the authentication type as OAuth2 . Paste the OAUTH_CLIENT_ID into Client ID and the OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET into Client Secret , then click Create Auth Config . Click Connect Account and enter your Snowflake account identifier in orgname-accountname format, for example myorg-account123 . In Snowsight, click your account in the bottom left and choose View account details to find it. Sign in to Snowflake, approve access, and confirm the account shows as Active . See Custom auth configs for the general flow. Scopes The default auth config requests the refresh_token scope, so Composio can refresh access without asking the user to sign in again. Snowflake roles, not OAuth scopes, decide which databases, schemas, and warehouses the connection can use. How do I configure roles and permissions for Snowflake? Ensure the OAuth app and Snowflake roles, databases, and schemas are configured correctly for the integration. Does Snowflake require per-user OAuth credentials? Yes. Snowflake OAuth is tied to the user's Snowflake account and security integration. There is not a single generic Snowflake OAuth app that can safely cover every account, role setup, redirect URI, and security policy. For a production integration, each Snowflake user should bring the OAuth client credentials from the security integration configured in their own Snowflake account. Create a Composio auth config with those credentials, then let the user connect with the account identifier and permissions for that Snowflake account. This keeps the connection aligned with the user's Snowflake roles, databases, schemas, and refresh-token policy.
